draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: After many corrections, the conversation can become a pile of local repairs while no external check protects the original whole job.
causalSequence: Each new correction reacts to the latest output and can compete with, duplicate or obscure earlier requirements.
An acknowledgement only shows that the model generated an acknowledgement; it does not enforce the rule or prove the next artifact complies.
An external brief, versioned best artifact and rerunnable checks let each bounded revision earn promotion without abandoning the long job.

evidenceAnalysis.claimUnderInspection: After enough corrections, the only practical fix is to start a new session with a cleaner prompt.
evidenceAnalysis.establishes: OpenAI says long sessions can amplify repeated prompt/tool content and recommends lean instructions, representative tasks, one bounded change at a time and rerunning the same evaluations.
evidenceAnalysis.doesNotEstablish: That every long conversation fails, that all products manage context identically or that external tests guarantee universal reliability.
evidenceAnalysis.claimedImpact: A clean session is the universal recovery for instruction drift.
evidenceAnalysis.realConsequence: A context refresh can sometimes help, but durable recovery comes from external truth, versioning and checks that survive the session.
evidenceAnalysis.aidbReason: A repository search of recent AIDB records on August 11 found no conflicting treatment of this exact repeated-revision failure; current official guidance and Ali's observed production incident govern the bounded answer.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating the rejected advice to start a new session or write more instructions while ignoring long-job reality and unenforced controls.

representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A newcomer can explain why repeated corrections drift and can recover the same long job without relying on memory, apology or a universal restart.
